sources.title: Jacqueline Stedall, Early Probability, Oxford Academic
Stephen M. Stigler, Is probability easier now than in 1560? (2015)
David Bellhouse, Decoding Cardano’s Liber de Ludo Aleae (2005)
ETH Zurich Library, From Games of Chance to Probability Theory

claims.statement: Cardano's Liber de Ludo Aleae is a 16th-century manuscript published after his death in 1663
claims.caution: Writing year disputed: sources say circa 1526 or circa 1560; do not assign a unique composition year

claims.statement: Cardano correctly tabulated ordinary sum counts for two and three dice
claims.caution: Not to claim he introduced modern sample-space notation

claims.statement: Two equiprobable independent six-faced dice have 36 ordered outcomes; sum five has four and sum seven has six
At least one specified face in two dice corresponds to 11/36; in three dice it corresponds to 91/216
claims.caution: Not a quotation of Cardano; complement counts must exclude overlaps

claims.statement: Cardano made errors on harder subset-sum dice conditions, which Stigler discusses
claims.caution: No modern-error correction is attributed to historical author

claims.statement: Bellhouse interprets Cardano's treatise through justice and knowledge traditions
Publication in 1663 limits direct impact on Fermat/Pascal's 1654 correspondence
claims.caution: Does not imply no influence from other earlier arithmetic traditions

claims.statement: Prior mathematical dice enumerations existed in medieval sources
claims.caution: Do not claim Cardano invented dice enumeration
